ITEMS.TRANSCRIPT_TEXT: Ça peut aller jusqu'où ? Jusqu'à bloquer Paris ? C'est ce que vous dites au Premier ministre ce matin ? On l'a déjà fait, le but, ça ne serait pas d'y arriver parce que ce qui est dramatique c'est que s'il faut en arriver là, ça va devenir usant dans ce pays, s'il faut toujours être en train de bloquer un pays. Mais sauf que s'il le faut, vous le ferez ? Si il le faut, potentiellement on y réfléchira et on le fera, mais on concertera notre réseau parce que c'est notre réseau qui est en action, qui est sur le terrain, et on verra avec eux. Mais s'il faut en arriver là, oui on l'a déjà fait, donc on peut le refaire. La détermination en tout cas elle est bien réelle sur le terrain ? Je pense que plus que jamais, moi je l'ai jamais vu à un niveau si élevé. Jamais ? Non. Jamais par le passé ? Non, non, là honnêtement on a une vraie crise profonde. Les mecs, malheureusement, pour certains plus rien à perdre. Donc en fait c'est leur survie qui est en jeu, leur survie de leurs entreprises, leur famille. Donc voilà, il y a des gens déterminés qui ne lâcheront rien. Le risque, disent certains, c'est une gilet jaunisation de ce mouvement. C'est ce que vous redoutez ? On peut toujours le redouter après moi j'ai confiance en nos agriculteurs qui sont des gens responsables, qui sont des chefs d'entreprise. Mais la colère elle est là. Oui la colère est là. Il faut aussi qu'on fasse attention à pas qu'il y ait des gens qui profitent du mouvement pour venir s'y raccrocher. Penser à certains politiques ? Oui. Rassemblement national par exemple ? Oui comme d'autres, il y a un moment donné moi je veux bien qu'ils nous aiment tous tant mieux mais qu'ils le prouvent par des actes, à un moment donné les paroles ça suffit.

ITEMS.CAPTION_TEXT:
Marijke Vanderlaan, Agronomic Service Representative, is training for an endurance mountain bike race - and she sees a lot of parallels with growing wheat. If she doesn’t build up muscle biomass leading up to the race day, she won’t survive the race. The same goes for wheat, grain fill period is like race day for your wheat crop and what you do BEFORE that period matters even more.⁣
⁣
In part two of her conversation with Lyndsey Smith, Host at @realagriculture, she breaks down why there's a big difference between growth stage 31 and 32, how pushing your fungicide timing a bit later can give you more value, and why maximizing the grain fill period is the ultimate goal. One extra grain fill day can mean three to four more bushels.⁣
⁣
Watch the full interview at the #LinkInBio

ITEMS.TRANSCRIPT_TEXT: So there's two things here. One is, I just want to send a shout out to wheat that the reason it's considered a rotation crop is by adding it, you do get benefits to your corn and beans. So just putting it out there. But also, Marika, and that's more of what we're tackling today is of course, it does respond to management. So you've outlined maybe some of the things that we know that the year after year, especially with something like the Yen Project, we see that come through. But what about for those growers that, you know, are paying attention to their planting date, maybe have adjusted it, they know about sulfur, what else could they focus on to really push this crop? Yeah, and I think that too, like I had the opportunity to go to the UK last spring and meet some really amazing growers. probably you have boots on the ground already if you're managing your wheat crop more intensively, but dial in even further. Like there's a big difference between growth stage 31 and 32. We're going to get more bang for our buck out of that fungicide if we push it a little bit later. And I know a lot of folks are even thinking about does three passes of fungicide matter? And sometimes it can. In a heavy stripe rust environment, yes it can. In a heavy powdery mildew environment, yes I really believe that it can. I think to some folks that are managing more intensively, they think, I'll just put that cheap fungicide on, that one mode of action product at that T1. But again, I'm a big believer in that Cadillac, that Miravis Neo at that T1 timing because... It was actually SWAC two years ago, Dr. Dave Hooker talked about your crop growth rate. And I was gonna say this earlier, one thing I'm also doing right now is I'm training for an endurance mountain bike race. And I was kind of thinking that the actual race day is like the grain fill period for your wheat crop. So what you do, like in, you know, for that t3 timing matters but what you do before then matters even more. Like my training like if I don't build that muscle biomass leading up to that day like I am not going to survive that race. And so I think you know for intensive growers thinking a lot more of what you're doing up till that grain fill period matters because if we can maximize that grain fill period one more day of grain fill can be three or four more bushels and obviously that matters.
